related_resources.reason: Early distinction between activities as ends and products as separate ends.
Distinguishes intrinsic, extrinsic, final and instrumental value with appropriate philosophical cautions.
Discusses meaningfulness independently of mere pleasure and moral rightness.
Definitions of play that attend to motives, rules and participant framing.

historical_claims.anchor: At the beginning of the Nicomachean Ethics, Aristotle distinguishes activities whose aims are in the doing from activities that produce something beyond the doing.
historical_claims.source_locator: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics I.1, 1094a1-18; public-domain Rackham translation

claim_evidence.anchor: A useful technical phrase is intrinsic value, though philosophers distinguish intrinsic value from other concepts such as final value, and they dispute exactly how the categories should be drawn.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Intrinsic vs. Extrinsic Value, overview and conceptual distinctions
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Terminology and disputes over kinds of value; the essay uses a simplified heuristic, not a canonical taxonomy.

claim_evidence.anchor: Scholars of play have long argued over how best to define it.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Peter Gray (2013), Definitions of Play, conceptual survey
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Different candidate characteristics include intrinsic motivation, freedom, structure and frame.

authorship.scope: Original philosophical essay. Historical philosophical attribution and terminology grounded in listed sources; beach scene and other illustrations are deliberately constructed.

background: No prior specialist knowledge; the distinction between a product and an activity as an end is explained.
readiness_checks: Explain why a sandcastle need not be judged by the requirements of a fortress.
Distinguish the value of an experience from a durable record or output.
Describe a case in which removing friction improves an activity and a case in which it defeats its purpose.
State why transience does not prove worthlessness without denying that losses are real.

description: Uses a sandcastle's deliberate impermanence to examine why worthwhile experiences need not last forever or serve a permanent practical purpose.
